🌿 First Camping Trip · Early October

Sonoma Camping Weekend

Redwoods, one night under the stars, a Russian River wine stop, and an apple orchard on the way home. First time camping, made easy.

Day 1 · Redwoods, Wine & Camp Day 2 · Hike, Apples & Home Good to Know

One night camping, kept intentionally simple since it's everyone's first time. Redwood hiking, one wine tasting (DD duty for Cali), campfire games, then a real hike, apple picking, and phenomenal croissants on the way home.

01

Redwoods, Wine & Camp

Saturday

A relaxed drive up, a real hike through ancient redwoods, one easy wine stop, then settling into camp for games and a campfire dinner.

Depart San Francisco

9:00–9:30am

~1.5hrs to Guerneville, no early alarm needed for this one.

Lunch — Mendocino Farms

10:30–11:15am

Santa Rosa, right on the way up. Healthy sandwiches, salads, and wraps made with fresh ingredients, real variety without needing a detour.

Hike — Armstrong Redwoods

12:00–2:00pm Easy · ~2-3mi

Armstrong Tree, Parson Jones Tree, and the Burbank Circle loop, 1,300+ year-old redwoods. Extend into Austin Creek if the group wants more mileage.

AllTrails: Armstrong Redwoods

Check In & Set Up Camp

2:15–3:00pm

Under the redwood canopy, real shade, quiet, peaceful, no radios or generators allowed here.

🍷 Half a mile down the road

Pee Wee Golf and Arcade

3:15–4:30pm Since the 1940s

Quirky, redwood-themed mini golf right in town. Playful, low-key, no pressure, a fun stop between the hike and camp.

Free Time & Showers

4:30–6:00pm

River, hammocks, coin-op showers (bring quarters), whatever the group wants.

Dinner — Korean BBQ at Camp

6:00–7:00pm On the fire grate

Every site here has a built-in fire ring with a flip-down metal grill grate, confirmed, no portable grill needed. Marinated meat straight on the grate, plus chicken, a pre-packaged salad, and pre-cut fruit on the side. Bring a small cast-iron skillet or heavy-duty foil if you want more of a flat-top for thinner cuts. Paper plates keep cleanup easy.

Campfire Games — Skull

7:00–9:30pm

A bluffing/strategy game built for small groups, plays great at exactly 5. Bold, simple cards mean it still works fine by lantern light once it gets dark. Quick rounds, real strategy, easy to learn on the spot. Backup for later: Wavelength, mostly verbal so it is even more forgiving of low light. S'mores and stargazing after, download a stargazing app before you lose signal. Quiet campground, so keep it acoustic, no speakers.

Tonight's Stay
Schoolhouse Canyon Campground
Guerneville, CA
02

Hike, Apples & Home

Sunday

A real hike with forest and coastal views, then apple picking and phenomenal croissants on the way home. No rush, lunch can wait until you're back.

Slow Morning & Pack Up

Wake up → 9:30am

Coffee, breakfast at camp, pack up before heading out so there's no rush after the hike.

🚗 ~25 min to Willow Creek Rd

Hike — Pomo Canyon Trail to Red Hill

10:15am–12:45pm Moderate · 3.5mi

Starts shaded in redwood and cedar forest with ferns, opens into coastal grassland, ends with panoramic ocean and Russian River views at the summit.

AllTrails: Pomo Canyon to Red Hill
🚗 ~20 min to Duncans Mills

Duncans Mills

1:05–1:35pm Tiny historic village

Under 200 people, real Old West charm. Gold Coast Coffee & Bakery for locally roasted coffee and their well-loved cinnamon rolls, plus a tea shop, art gallery, and antique shops to wander. Right on the way, not a detour.

🚗 ~35 min to Sebastopol

Apple & Pear Picking — Ratzlaff Ranch

2:10–2:55pm $2/lb

Family-run since nearly a century, U-pick runs mid-September through October, perfect timing. Gravenstein, Golden Delicious, and Rome apples, plus pears too, both available the same visit. Grab their apple cider while you are there. Call ahead to confirm picking availability.

🍫 Right next door, same road

Pumpkin Picking — Papa's Pumpkin Patch

2:55–3:25pm Peak season

Seven varieties, pick straight off the vine, all set in the shade of old-growth redwoods, right next door to the orchard. Open daily in October, 9am–4pm, no reservation needed.

🚗 A few minutes away

Croissants — Patisserie Angelica

3:30–4:00pm Best in Sonoma County

Daily almond croissants, organic ingredients, a genuinely respected French patisserie, specifically called out in Sonoma Magazine's best-croissants roundup. Closer than Healdsburg's Quail & Condor, and just as worth it.

🚗 ~1.5 hrs home

Arrive Home

~5:30–5:45pm No rush

Lunch can wait, eat at home whenever, or snack on fresh apples the whole way back.

Good to Know

First Time Camping

Kept to one night on purpose, low-risk way to find out if the group loves it before committing to more nights next time.

Showers

Coin-operated at Schoolhouse Canyon, bring quarters. Clean, reliable, worth it after a day of hiking.

Quiet Campground

No radios or generators allowed, keeps it peaceful. Plan games and music accordingly, acoustic only.

Cell Service

Spotty at Armstrong Redwoods and Pomo Canyon. Download offline maps and a stargazing app before you lose signal.

Pack Layers

Warm days, genuinely cool nights under the redwood canopy. A real jacket earns its space.

Apple Picking Timing

Ratzlaff Ranch U-pick runs mid-September through October, call ahead to confirm they're picking that day before driving over.

Redwoods, one campfire, apples on the way home. — Cali's Sonoma Camping Itinerary
